materials.cover_letter:
I build AI agents and the evaluation systems to know if they actually work. That is the job, and your posting for AI Agent Architect, Customer Experience describes exactly the work I have been doing.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI-powered content validation workflow with automated benchmarks and quality scoring. It reduced escalations by 70-80% by preventing incorrect output from reaching customers. I designed structured guardrails, fallback paths, and post-processing checks to catch hallucinations before they caused harm. I also automated a documentation pipeline and built a PDF system that resolved a years-long customer complaint.

Your posting asks for someone to own retrieval accuracy, drive automated resolution rates, manage AI safety, and own the feedback loop. I have done exactly that. I would welcome the conversation.

short_answers.Why this company?: I'm drawn to Airtable's mission of empowering teams through flexible, scalable tools. The AI Agent Architect role sits at the intersection of content architecture, AI safety, and customer experience—exactly where my expertise in building trusted AI workflows and knowledge systems lies. I'm excited to apply my experience with guardrails and retrieval accuracy to help Airtable deliver reliable, high-resolution customer experiences.
short_answers.Tell us about yourself: I'm an AI Workflow Engineer and Technical Writer with 7+ years of experience at companies like Redwood, Attentive, and Bird. I specialize in building knowledge systems and AI-driven workflows that increase automation while maintaining trust and accuracy. At Redwood, I architected FlareGuard, an AI content validation workflow that cut escalations by 70–80%, and redesigned a 200-article help portal for role-aware navigation. I'm passionate about designing auditable, predictable systems that improve retrieval precision and keep AI agents safe and effective—both of which I see as central to this role.
